plan.notes: Transcribed 2026-11-14 from the official Salem College 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (current edition, catoid=34), Public Health (BA) program page (poid=930). Salem College publishes major requirements but no official semester sequence for this program (its Print Degree Planner is a blank worksheet), so the plan is collected in requirements_only form as a single block. The full degree requirements, including the Salem Impact core (published separately in the same catalog), are not itemized here. Per-course credits are the Hour(s) values printed on each course's own official course detail page in the same catalog; the program page itself prints no per-course credits. Prerequisites naming courses outside this plan are disclosed in these notes and are not recorded as plan prerequisites. The introduction states the degree requires 61-62 credit hours; the recorded total (61) is the exact itemized sum at the minimum path: Public Health Core 33 (eleven courses at 3) + Scientific Inquiry 4 + Ethics 3 + Statistics 3 (block printed 3-4 hrs; exercised at 3 via PSYC 201 -- a 4-hour statistics completion totals 62) + Interdisciplinary 15 + Experiential Learning 3 itemized. DISCLOSED catalog heading error: the Experiential Learning block is headed '(6 hrs)' but its two courses itemize to 3 (PUBH 360 at 2 Hour(s) + PUBH 370 at 1 Hour(s)); the printed degree total of 61-62 reconciles only at the itemized 3 (at 6 the blocks would sum to 64-65), so the itemized value is recorded and the heading disclosed, not corrected. The Interdisciplinary block prints no hour total and no choose wording; it is read as five slots -- COMM 275, POLI 105 and POLI 224 as fixed courses, plus the two printed OR pairs (NUTR 210 / EXER 210, then NUTR 225 / BCHM 225) each counted once at 3 -- the reading under which the printed degree total reconciles exactly; the page does not state whether the OR sits within each pair, between the pairs, or both, and that ambiguity is disclosed here. Residency as printed: students must complete 5 of the 11 Core Public Health classes and both Experiential Learning classes (PUBH 360 and PUBH 370) at Salem. Prerequisites recorded only where every named course is a fixed course in this plan: PUBH 210 requires BIOL 100; PUBH 350 requires PUBH 100; PUBH 330 requires PUBH 100, PUBH 250, PUBH 300 and PUBH 320. Disclosed, not recorded: PUBH 250 and PUBH 300 each also require one of the statistics courses (MATH 107 or PSYC 201 or BIOL 205 or INTG 115), a one-of prerequisite exercised through this plan's statistics slot; the statistics options' own prerequisites name MATH courses outside this plan (see the statistics slot). PUBH 360 and PUBH 370 are printed as mutual corequisites and are recorded as corequisites; PUBH 370's description notes a 120-hour field experience. BIOL 100's printed corequisite BIOL 100L (0 Hour(s)) is disclosed here and not placed, per the Salem lab precedent. PUBH 320's description recommends previous coursework in Public Health or a related field; a recommendation is not a printed Prerequisite(s) line. Anomalies transcribed as printed: PUBH 260's title is spelled 'Intoduction to Global Health' on the program page and its detail page (the Print Degree Planner spells it 'Introduction to Global Health'); PUBH 350's title is truncated as printed ('Administration of Public Health Organiz') on the program page, its detail page and the planner, and no fuller title is printed anywhere in this catalog edition. The program page also states that students completing this program are eligible to take the Certified Health Education Specialist (CHES) exam.

courses.title: Determinants of Health and Health Equity
Cell and Molecular Biology with Lab
Ethics Elective
courses.choice_note: Choose one course for the Ethics requirement (3 hrs), as printed. Both catalog options are printed at 3 Hour(s) and are listed.

courses.title: Statistics Elective
courses.choice_note: Choose one statistics course, as printed. Recorded at the block's printed minimum of 3 Hour(s) via the listed option, PSYC 201 (3 Hour(s)). The remaining catalog options are printed at 4 Hour(s) and are disclosed here, not listed as fixed options (Salem differing-credit precedent): MATH 107 Statistical Methods with R (prerequisite: MATH 060 or MATH 070 or MATH 100), BIOL 205 Biological Statistics (prerequisite: MATH 025 or MATH 070 or MATH 100; corequisite BIOL 205L, 0 Hour(s), disclosed not placed), and INTG 115 Statistical Inference (prerequisite: MATH 020). A completion using a 4-hour statistics course totals 62, the top of the program's printed 61-62 credit hours. The named prerequisites of the statistics options are outside this plan and are disclosed here, not recorded.

courses.title: Nutrition Elective
courses.choice_note: One course from the printed NUTR 210 / EXER 210 pair in the Interdisciplinary block, counted once. The listed option is NUTR 210 (3 Hour(s)). The pair's other printed code, EXER 210 Introduction to Nutrition (3 Hour(s)), is the same course under its cross-listed code; EXER 210's own detail page states the EXER 210 course code is being removed and all EXER 210 listings should be replaced with NUTR 210, so the slot is recorded under NUTR 210 with the printed pair disclosed here. NUTR 210's description recommends one of CHEM 110, BIOL 010, BIOL 065 or BIOL 100 as a prerequisite; a recommendation is not a printed Prerequisite(s) line and is disclosed here, not recorded.

courses.title: Diet and Disease Elective
courses.choice_note: One course from the printed NUTR 225 / BCHM 225 pair in the Interdisciplinary block, counted once. The two codes are cross-listed as printed (each detail page names the other) and both are printed at 3 Hour(s), so both are listed. Their descriptions recommend either NUTR 210, CHEM 110, BIOL 010, BIOL 065 or BIOL 100; a recommendation is not a printed Prerequisite(s) line and is disclosed here, not recorded. BCHM 225's detail description is printed twice in succession in the catalog, as printed.
